query: Which material can be used for ductility, and why?

generation.hypothesis: If a CoCrFeNi-based high-entropy alloy is lightly alloyed with aluminum (e.g., Al0.1CoCrFeNi), the resulting predominantly face-centered-cubic phase will exhibit enhanced ductility compared to alloys with higher aluminum content that form brittle ordered or body-centered-cubic phases.
generation.material_initial_state: A near-equiatomic, quaternary CoCrFeNi alloy with an FCC solid-solution microstructure.
generation.intervention: Partial substitution of Ni or Fe by small fractions of Al (around 0.1 atomic ratio) within the CoCrFeNi matrix.
generation.conditions: Separate melt casting of samples with different Al contents, followed by standard heat treatment to ensure microstructural homogeneity, then tensile testing at room and moderate temperatures (20–600°C). Structural analysis with SEM, TEM, and XRD at each composition and temperature.
generation.structural_mediator: Retention of a single FCC solid-solution phase at low Al content; avoidance of brittle B2 or bcc phases.
generation.mechanism: Low-to-moderate Al content refines the stacking fault energy and stabilizes an FCC lattice, enabling more uniform dislocation slip and delaying crack formation, thereby improving ductility.
generation.predicted_outcome: A significant increase in elongation-to-failure with minimal loss in strength, resulting in a superior combination of ductility and strength in the Al0.1CoCrFeNi alloy versus higher-Al variants.
generation.baseline: Equiatomic CoCrFeNi without Al additions, which provides moderate ductility and strength at room temperature.
generation.boundary: When Al content exceeds a threshold (e.g., around 1.0 atomic ratio), the formation of B2 and bcc phases impairs ductility despite potential higher strength.
generation.uncertainty: Precise optimal Al addition for maximum ductility has not been fully established and may depend on other elemental variations or processing conditions.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize a series of AlxCoCrFeNi alloys with x ranging from 0 to 1.5 in increments (e.g., 0, 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5). Perform identical casting and homogenization, followed by microstructural characterization and tensile tests across a range of temperatures.
measurements: SEM/TEM for microstructural features (phase fractions, grain size, dislocation structures)
Tensile testing to determine yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and fracture elongation
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If Al0.1CoCrFeNi does not show improved ductility compared to both the Al-free and higher-Al alloys under these conditions, the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text:
High-entropy alloys (HEAs) are defined as equimolar or nonequimolar single- and multiphase solid solutions, depending on the number and type of principal/secondary metallic elements with the configurational entropy greater than 1.61 R , (where R is the gas constant) ( [1] , [2] ). The minimization of the Gibbs free energy by increasing the configurational entropy results in the formation of a single- or multiphase solid solution, such as body-centered cubic (BCC) ( [3] ), face-centered cubic (FCC) ( [4] ), and/or hexagonal close-packed solid-solution phases ( [5] ) instead of intermetallic compounds ( [6] ). Moreover, the random distribution of multiple elements with different atomic radii leads to a severely distorted lattice with variations in the interatomic distances along the crystallographic direction of the unit cells ( [3] ). These features, in turn, contribute to desirable mechanical properties, such as high hardness, strength, ductility, and softening resistance at room temperature (RT) and elevated temperatures ( [3] ).

Alloy ingots with a nominal composition of Al x CoCrFeNi ( x = 0.1, 0.75 and 1.5) were synthesized by arc-melting a mixture of pure metals (purity >99.6 wt.%) in a Ti-gettered high-purity argon atmosphere. These ingots were remelted at least four times to ensure chemical homogeneity. Melted alloys were eventually drop-cast into a mold Φ 5 × 70 mm 3 . The solidified ingots were cut into thin pieces 1 mm thick and one side polished. The sample densities for x = 0.1, 0.75 and 1.5, which were measured by Archimedes method, are 8.1, 7.4 and 6.9 g·cm −3 , respectively. The microstructures of as-prepared Al x CoCrFeNi HEAs ( x = 0.1, 0.75 and 1.5) are single fcc, fcc plus ordered bcc (B2) and B2 plus disordered bcc (A2), respectively.
